10.12.2024 Vide order dated 22.11.2022, petitioner was admitted to interim bail and since investigation of the present case has already concluded and it is only presentation of challan which is awaited, therefore, interim order dated 22.11.2022 is made absolute.

Bail App No.283/2022 is disposed of.
01.

Petitioner has invoked inherent jurisdiction of this Court in terms of Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1989 ('Cr.P.C.', for short) for quashment of FIR No. 0181/2022 registered with Police Station, Kishtwar, for alleged commission of offence under Sections 452/376/506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ['the IPC'], primarily on the ground of false implication.

It is case of the petitioner that he came into contact with respondent No.2, they fell in love and respondent No.2 in order to marry him converted to Islam and solemnized the Nikah as per Shariat Laws on 19.07.2022.
According to the petitioner, his relationship with respondent No.2 is consensual.
However, it is alleged that the complainant-respondent No.2 started extorting money from him and lodged the impugned FIR as a tool of harassment.

02. It is trite that inherent jurisdiction vested in the High Court, under Section 482 Cr.P.C., is to be exercised sparingly, with the circumspection and only to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court or to secure the ends of justice.

Reference in this respect may be made to 'Madhav Lamaye V.
State of Maharashtra'; AIR 1978 SC 47.

sentences.text: 03. As factual narration of the case, from the status report would unfurl, on 05.06.2022 a written complaint came to be preferred by respondent No.2 in the Court of learned Munsiff/JMIC, Kishtwar under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., which was forwarded to the concerned Police Station.

It was alleged that the complainant after some matrimonial dispute with her husband started living in a rental accommodation at Gurian along with her children and on 16-17th May 2022 at about 22.00 Hrs, the petitioner barged into the house of the complainant and raped her throughout night by threatening her for life.
On the basis of this complaint, impugned FIR came to be registered against the petitioner.
The investigating Agency has already got medical report of the victim/complainant and her statement has been recorded before the concerned Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
As per the status report, investigation of the present case has concluded and presentation of the challan is awaited.

Since the latest status report dated 17.05.2023 prima facie discloses the commission of offences against the petitioner under Sections 452/376/506 IPC, the present petition is found bereft of merit, hence, dismissed.
04. All interim orders shall stand vacated and the Investigating Agency shall be at liberty to present final report in the competent Court of law.
CRM(M) No.642/2022 is, accordingly, disposed of.

(Rajesh Sekhri) Judge JAMMU 10.12.2024 Eva Mohd. Yousif vs Ut Of J&K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123714197/
